name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q01 - Comprehensive evaluation of male reproductive anatomy

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements regarding the human male reproductive system:

Statement I: The scrotum maintains the temperature of the testes \(2\text{--}2.5\,^\circ\text{C}\) lower than normal internal body temperature for spermatogenesis.

Statement II: Each testis has about \(250\) testicular lobules, and each lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules.

Statement III: Sertoli cells line the inside of seminiferous tubules to nourish germ cells, whereas Leydig cells lie in the interstitial spaces and secrete androgens.

Statement IV: The male sex accessory ducts transport sperms from the seminiferous tubules sequentially through rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, and vas deferens.

Statement V: Seminal plasma is secreted exclusively by the seminal vesicles and is devoid of fructose and calcium.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The male reproductive system consists of paired testes, accessory ducts, accessory glands, and external genitalia working together to produce, nourish, store, and deliver sperms.

Step 2: Evaluation of Testicular Structure and Cells
Situating the testes in the scrotum keeps their temperature \(2\text{--}2.5\,^\circ\text{C}\) below internal body temperature, which is essential for spermatogenesis. Each testis contains roughly \(250\) testicular lobules, each housing one to three coiled seminiferous tubules lined internally by spermatogonia and nutritive Sertoli cells, while interstitial Leydig cells outside the tubules secrete androgens.

Step 3: Evaluation of Accessory Ducts and Seminal Plasma
Sperms travel from the seminiferous tubules through the rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, and vas deferens before joining the seminal vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct entering the urethra. However, seminal plasma is produced collectively by the paired seminal vesicles, prostate gland, and paired bulbourethral glands, and it is rich in fructose, calcium, and certain enzymes—making the claim that it comes solely from seminal vesicles without fructose or calcium false.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The four claims covering scrotal thermoregulation, testicular lobule and tubule counts, Sertoli and Leydig cell locations and roles, and the sequential accessory duct pathway are correct, whereas the claim restricting seminal plasma to seminal vesicles and denying its fructose and calcium content is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II and III only
Statements I, III, IV and V only
Statements II, III, IV and V only
Statements I, II, III and IV only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q02 - Female reproductive tract and mammary gland synthesis

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following five statements regarding the human female reproductive system and mammary glands:

Statement I: Each ovary is \(2\text{--}4\text{ cm}\) long, covered by a thin epithelium enclosing ovarian stroma divided into a peripheral cortex and an inner medulla.

Statement II: The fallopian tube extends from the ovary to the uterus via the infundibulum (bearing fimbriae), the wider ampulla, and the narrow-lumened isthmus.

Statement III: In the uterine wall, the perimetrium undergoes cyclical menstrual changes while the endometrium exhibits strong contractions during delivery.

Statement IV: The hymen is always torn only during the first coitus and never persists afterwards, making it a reliable indicator of virginity.

Statement V: In each mammary gland, alveoli secrete milk into alveolar lumens, which passes through mammary tubules, mammary ducts, mammary ampulla, and the lactiferous duct.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The female reproductive system and mammary glands are structurally organised to support ovulation, gamete transport, gestation, childbirth, and lactation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ovary, Oviduct, and Mammary Ductal Pathway
Each ovary measures \(2\text{--}4\text{ cm}\) in length with a thin epithelial covering and stroma partitioned into a peripheral cortex and inner medulla. Each \(10\text{--}12\text{ cm}\) oviduct comprises the fimbriae-bearing infundibulum near the ovary, the wider ampulla, and the narrow-lumened isthmus joining the uterus. In the mammary glands, milk from alveoli travels sequentially through mammary tubules, mammary ducts, mammary ampulla, and the lactiferous duct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Uterine Wall Layers and Hymen
In the uterine wall, the inner glandular endometrium undergoes cyclical changes during the menstrual cycle, whereas the middle smooth-muscle myometrium contracts strongly during delivery—not the outer membranous perimetrium or the endometrium. Furthermore, the hymen can break due to falls, jolts, tampons, or sports such as cycling and horseback riding, and may persist after coitus, so it is not a reliable indicator of virginity or sexual experience.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The three claims describing ovarian dimensions and stroma, fallopian tube segmentation, and the mammary milk-ejection ductal pathway are correct, whereas the claims swapping uterine wall layer functions and treating the hymen as a reliable indicator of virginity are incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II and III only
Statements I, II and V only
Statements II, III and V only
Statements I, II, IV and V only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q03 - Gametogenesis hormones sperm fertility and oogenesis

questiontext.text:
Examine the following five statements regarding human gametogenesis:

Statement I: In spermatogenesis, \(\text{LH}\) acts on Leydig cells to stimulate androgen synthesis, whereas \(\text{FSH}\) acts on Sertoli cells to stimulate secretion of factors aiding spermiogenesis.

Statement II: For normal fertility in human males, at least \(60\%\) of the \(200\text{--}300\) million ejaculated sperms must have normal shape and size and at least \(40\%\) must show vigorous motility.

Statement III: In females, oogonia continue to divide and are newly added to the ovary after birth until puberty.

Statement IV: At puberty, only \(60,000\text{--}80,000\) primary follicles remain in each ovary due to degeneration between birth and puberty.

Statement V: Within the tertiary follicle, the primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division equally to form two equal-sized haploid secondary oocytes.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Spermatogenesis and oogenesis are regulated by pituitary gonadotropins and involve distinct cellular reserves and meiotic division symmetry.

Step 2: Evaluation of Male Hormonal Control, Fertility Criteria, and Ovarian Reserve
During spermatogenesis, \(\text{LH}\) stimulates Leydig cells to secrete androgens, while \(\text{FSH}\) acts on Sertoli cells to release factors supporting spermiogenesis. Normal male fertility requires at least \(60\%\) of ejaculated sperms to have normal morphology and at least \(40\%\) to show vigorous motility. In females, follicular degeneration from birth to puberty reduces the ovarian reserve to \(60,000\text{--}80,000\) primary follicles per ovary at puberty.

Step 3: Evaluation of Postnatal Oogonia and Meiosis I Symmetry
No new oogonia are formed or added after birth; all oogonia are produced during fetal life. Furthermore, when the primary oocyte completes meiosis I inside the tertiary follicle, the division is unequal—producing one large haploid secondary oocyte that retains most of the nutrient-rich cytoplasm and one tiny first polar body, rather than two equal-sized secondary oocytes.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims concerning \(\text{LH}\) and \(\text{FSH}\) target cells, male sperm morphology and motility thresholds, and the \(60,000\text{--}80,000\) primary follicle reserve at puberty are correct, whereas the claims of postnatal oogonia addition and equal first meiotic division in oogenesis are incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II and IV only
Statements I, III and IV only
Statements II, IV and V only
Statements I, II, IV and V only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q04 - Menstrual cycle regulation and fertilisation events

questiontext.text:
Analyse the following six statements regarding the menstrual cycle and fertilisation in humans:

Statement I: Cyclic menstruation extends between menarche at puberty and menopause around \(50\) years of age, with an average cycle interval of \(28/29\) days.

Statement II: The menstrual phase lasts \(3\text{--}5\) days and results from breakdown of the uterine endometrium and its blood vessels when the released ovum is not fertilised.

Statement III: Rapid secretion of \(\text{LH}\) at mid-cycle (about day \(14\)), called the \(\text{LH}\) surge, induces rupture of the Graafian follicle and ovulation.

Statement IV: After ovulation, the corpus luteum secretes progesterone, and if fertilisation fails, the corpus luteum persists permanently to prevent the next cycle.

Statement V: Fertilisation occurs in the ampullary region only when the ovum and sperms are transported there simultaneously, and sperm contact with the zona pellucida blocks entry of additional sperms.

Statement VI: Sperm entry into the oocyte cytoplasm halts meiosis II permanently so that the secondary oocyte fuses directly with the sperm nucleus.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The menstrual cycle prepares the female reproductive tract for fertilisation and implantation through sequential pituitary-ovarian hormone shifts, while fertilisation requires simultaneous gamete arrival, polyspermy prevention, and completion of oocyte meiosis II.

Step 2: Evaluation of Menstrual Cycle Dynamics
Normal cyclic menstruation spans from menarche to menopause (around \(50\) years) at roughly \(28/29\)-day intervals. Menstrual bleeding for \(3\text{--}5\) days occurs due to endometrial breakdown when fertilisation does not happen. Mid-cycle \(\text{LH}\) surge around day \(14\) ruptures the Graafian follicle to release the ovum, after which the corpus luteum secretes progesterone. However, in the absence of fertilisation, the corpus luteum degenerates rather than persisting, causing endometrial disintegration and starting a new menstrual cycle.

Step 3: Evaluation of Fertilisation Events
Simultaneous transport of ovum and sperms to the ampullary region is required for fertilisation, and sperm contact with the zona pellucida induces membrane changes that block polyspermy. Upon entering the oocyte cytoplasm, the sperm induces completion (not halting) of the unequal second meiotic division, forming a second polar body and a haploid ovum (ootid) whose nucleus then fuses with the sperm nucleus.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The four claims covering the menarche-to-menopause reproductive span, \(3\text{--}5\) day endometrial breakdown, mid-cycle \(\text{LH}\) surge ovulation, and simultaneous ampullary arrival with zona pellucida polyspermy block are correct, whereas the claims that the corpus luteum persists without fertilisation and that sperm entry halts meiosis II are incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III and IV only
Statements I, III, V and VI only
Statements I, II, III and V only
Statements II, III, IV and V only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_MCQ_Q05 - Cleavage placenta fetal milestones and parturition

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following six statements covering human post-fertilisation development, pregnancy, and childbirth:

Statement I: Mitotic cleavage of the zygote in the isthmus forms blastomeres, with the \(8\text{--}16\) blastomere stage called the morula, which later transforms into the blastocyst containing an outer trophoblast and an inner cell mass.

Statement II: Chorionic villi on the trophoblast interdigitate with uterine tissue to form the placenta, which connects to the embryo via the umbilical cord for exchange of gases, nutrients, and wastes.

Statement III: Hormones such as \(\text{hCG}\), \(\text{hPL}\), and relaxin are produced in women throughout their non-pregnant reproductive cycles as well as during pregnancy.

Statement IV: The inner cell mass differentiates into ectoderm, endoderm, and mesoderm, and contains stem cells potent enough to give rise to all tissues and organs.

Statement V: During human gestation, the embryo's heart forms after one month, limbs and digits by the end of the second month, and first foetal movements with head hair appear during the fifth month.

Statement VI: Parturition is triggered by the foetal ejection reflex and oxytocin feedback, whereas colostrum is secreted only at the end of the sixth month after childbirth.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Post-fertilisation events progress from cleavage and blastocyst implantation to placental formation, germ-layer organogenesis along a defined \(9\)-month timeline, and oxytocin-driven parturition followed by colostrum secretion.

Step 2: Evaluation of Cleavage, Placenta, Germ Layers, and Foetal Milestones
Cleavage forms a morula (\(8\text{--}16\) blastomeres) and then a blastocyst with an outer trophoblast and inner cell mass. Chorionic villi interdigitate with uterine tissue to form the placenta linked to the embryo by the umbilical cord. The inner cell mass differentiates into ectoderm, endoderm, and mesoderm and houses pluripotent stem cells. Developmentally, the heart forms after one month, limbs and digits by the end of the second month, and first foetal movements and head hair appear in the fifth month.

Step 3: Evaluation of Pregnancy-Specific Hormones and Colostrum Timing
Human chorionic gonadotropin (\(\text{hCG}\)), human placental lactogen (\(\text{hPL}\)), and relaxin are produced in women exclusively during pregnancy—never during non-pregnant cycles. Additionally, while parturition is indeed driven by the foetal ejection reflex and positive oxytocin feedback, colostrum is the antibody-rich milk produced during the initial few days of lactation immediately after childbirth, not at the end of the sixth month.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The four claims describing morula and blastocyst formation, placental and umbilical cord function, germ-layer differentiation with stem cells, and the first-, second-, and fifth-month developmental milestones are accurate, whereas the claims regarding non-pregnant \(\text{hCG}/\text{hPL}/\text{relaxin}\) production and sixth-month colostrum secretion are incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III and V only
Statements I, II, IV and V only
Statements I, IV, V and VI only
Statements II, III, IV and VI only
